# Course workflow — issues, PRs, reviews, sprint deliverables

Course rules, not upstream Gitea ones. Source: the course site <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>
(Sprints pages) and `docs/sprint0/standards.md`. Everyone on the team, and every AI session, uses
the formats below so all issues and PRs look the same. The GitHub templates in `.github/` carry the
same formats; if they ever disagree with this page, fix the template.

AI disclosure has its own page: `AI-ASSISTANCE.md`.

## Current sprint: Sprint 2

- **Dates:** Oct 13 – Oct 29, 2026. Everything pushed and merged by **Oct 29, 11:59 PM**, except
  the D7 check-in, due **Oct 22, 11:59 PM**.
- **Points:** 100.
- **Zero rule:** no merged PR (D4), no sprint report (D8) or no release (D9) means **0 for the
  whole sprint**.
- **Carries forward:** anything the Sprint 2 page doesn't change comes from the Sprint 1 page, and
  every Sprint 0 standard still applies.

| # | Deliverable | Points | Who | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Sprint backlog: a `Sprint 2` milestone with every selected issue on it | 10 | Team | GitHub milestone |
| D2 | Requirements spec for each issue (formats below), peer-reviewed by a teammate before coding | 20 | Individual | Issue body |
| D3 | At least one non-trivial design decision per issue, with **at least two alternatives** | 5 | Individual | Issue body |
| D4 | Code changes and PRs, each with a `## Tech Debt` section | 20 | Individual | PRs |
| D5 | AI logs | 5 | Individual | `ai-logs/sprint2/<github-username>/` |
| D6 | UML class and sequence diagrams plus Q&A for one medium issue you resolved | 15 | Individual | `docs/sprint2/diagrams/` |
| D7 | Mid-sprint check-in | 5 | Individual | `docs/sprint2/checkin/<github-username>.md` |
| D8 | Sprint report | 10 | Team | `docs/sprint2/report.md` |
| D9 | Release: tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` plus a GitHub release | 2 | Team | Tags / Releases |
| D10 | Reflection survey | 8 | Individual | Blackboard/Zulip link |

- **D1 load:** each CSCI 435 student owns at least 2 medium issues; each CSCI 535 student owns at
  least 2 medium and 1 small. Either load can be met with equivalent story points instead. Every
  issue has exactly **one** assignee. Unfinished Sprint 1 issues
  go into the backlog before new work. To skip one, write the reason on that issue (closed, made
  invalid by later changes, or no longer relevant). If the backlog is too thin to meet the load,
  find areas that still need work (features, improvements, test gaps, bugs) and write new issues
  for them the usual way: user story, acceptance criteria and an estimate.
- **D3:** each decision names at least two concrete alternatives and why one won; this is graded
  strictly. The site also accepts the decision in an issue comment or the PR description; the team
  keeps it in the issue body. Decisions that span issues go in `docs/sprint2/design.md`.
- **D4:** every PR description has the Tech Debt section (see "Pull request format"). A PR without
  it loses points. Per-PR scores are combined across your issues and scaled to 20.
- **D5:** conventions are in `ai-logs/README.md`. Logs hold the full prompts and output: summaries,
  screenshots and share links are not logs. The link must open the log file itself, not a folder or
  another issue. The folder must exist even if no AI was used; in that case, post a comment saying
  so. The site accepts the link in an issue or a PR comment this sprint; the team keeps it in
  **issue comments only** (`AI-ASSISTANCE.md`).
- **D6:** see "UML diagrams (D6)" below.
- **D7:** about 150 words on each of: what you have done and what remains; one thing you learned
  about the codebase or about software engineering; one thing you would do differently. On time and
  substantive scores 5, late or thin 3, missing 0.
- **D8:** graded on completeness, specificity and quality of evidence; sections are in "Sprint
  report (D8) sections" below.
- **D9:** keep the base version (`v1.27.3-csci435-s1` → `v1.27.3-csci435-s2`), tag after every
  Sprint 2 PR is merged, push the tag to origin, and write release notes listing the features,
  fixes and improvements. The site's example says `v2.17.2`; this fork's base is `v1.27.3`.
- **Reviews:** nobody approves or merges their own PR. Reviewers leave substantive comments, not a
  bare approval. Tell the reviewer on Zulip or by email, and aim to review within 24 hours. Each
  student reviews at least one PR per sprint, and every teammate at least once per semester.
- **Extra credit:** up to 3 points per PR submitted to upstream Gitea that is accepted or under
  active review, at the instructor's discretion.

## Branches and commits

- Branches: `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` or
  `chore/short-description` (`STUDENTS.md`). One issue per branch.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and end with the issue number:
  `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page (#17)`. Add an
  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer when AI helped; never `Co-Authored-By` or
  `Signed-off-by` (`AGENTS.md`). A human approves every commit before it is made.

### Before each implementation: sync with main

Every new branch starts from an up-to-date `main`. AI sessions run this before writing any code:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/issue-<N>-short-description
```

To pick up new work on `main` for a branch that already exists, **merge, don't rebase**. Rebasing
or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/main
```

Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. Never merge another
feature branch into yours.

### After merge: clean up

A PR is merged with a merge commit once it is approved, every review comment is addressed and CI
passes. Then:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-<N>-short-description               # local branch
git push origin --delete feat/issue-<N>-short-description    # or GitHub's "Delete branch" button
git fetch --prune                                            # drop stale remote-tracking refs
```

Also check that the issue closed (via `Closes #N`), is on the sprint milestone, and has its AI
Assistance comment. Then run `specstory sync` and file the session's log (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

## Issue format: feature (user story)

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/user-story.yaml`. The user story must meet INVEST: Independent,
Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable.

```markdown
## User Story
As a <role>, I want <capability> so that <benefit>.

## User Scenario
<A short concrete walk-through: who, where in the UI, what they do, what they see.>

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given <state>, when <action>, then <observable result>.
- [ ] AC2: ...
- [ ] AC3: ...            (at least 3; each has a clear pass/fail result)

## Out of Scope
- <What this issue deliberately does not do.>

## Open Questions
- <Unresolved questions, or "None".>

## Design Decision
**Decision:** <what was chosen>
**Alternatives Considered:** <at least two concrete options, and why each lost>
**Rationale:** <why this one>
**Consequences:** <trade-offs, follow-up work, what it makes harder>

## Scope
small | medium | large, and matching `scope:` label
```

## Issue format: bug report

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug-report.yaml`.

```markdown
## Observed Behavior
## Expected Behavior
## Steps to Reproduce
1. ...
## Additional Information
<Version or commit, browser/OS, logs, screenshots.>
## Design Decision
<Same four fields as above: Decision, Alternatives Considered, Rationale, Consequences.>
```

- **Design Decision (D3):** fill it in once you've picked an approach, before opening the PR. Put
  a second decision under another `### Decision 2` heading. If a PR changes the decision, update
  the issue body.
- **Peer review (D2):** a teammate reads the spec and comments `Spec reviewed — <notes>` on the
  issue before implementation starts.

## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **How it was tested / Test strategy:** tests added or updated and why these ones. Name any
   change that can't be tested automatically and how it was checked by hand. Every behaviour change
   needs a new or updated test.
5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status, or the commands run and their results.
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **Tech Debt:** required from Sprint 2. Both fields are required, and `None.` is a valid answer:

   ```markdown
   ## Tech Debt

   **Introduced:** <shortcuts, workarounds or design compromises this PR makes, and why>

   **Encountered:** <tech debt that was already there and that you ran into, and how you handled it>
   ```

8. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6, test strategy with
explanation 5, description quality including the Tech Debt section 4, CI or manual verification 3,
review rubric posted 2.

## Code review rubric

The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.

```markdown
### Code Review — @reviewer-username

**Checked:** <what you ran or tried>

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |
```

## UML diagrams (D6)

The person who resolved a medium issue draws a class diagram and a sequence diagram for it. Several
small issues that together equal one medium issue are drawn together instead. Files:

- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<issue#>-<github-username>-class.png` (or `.pdf`)
- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<issue#>-<github-username>-sequence.png` (or `.pdf`)
- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<issue#>-<github-username>.md`, which embeds both and answers the Q&A

What the diagrams need:

- Show the existing code found during concept location and impact analysis, and the new or changed
  code, and tell the two apart with a legend, colour or label.
- Show only the fields and methods that matter to the issue.
- Annotate the diagrams with the key design decisions and calls. Diagrams without annotations lose
  points.
- Add a short note on how Go maps to UML: structs, interfaces, and embedding.
- The `.md` follows the course template: `# Issue #<N> -- <title>`, `## Class Diagram`,
  `## Sequence Diagram`, `## Q&A`, each diagram embedded with
  `![Class diagram](<issue#>-<github-username>-class.png)` under its heading. The Q&A has 3
  class-diagram questions, 3 sequence-diagram questions and 1 question on AI use, answered "N/A" if
  no AI was used. The questions, copied from the Sprint 2 page:

```markdown
**Class diagram:**

1. Among all the classes shown in the diagram, which 1--2 are most central to understanding the codebase and solving the issue? Explain what role each one plays.
2. What is the most significant relationship shown in the diagram? Explain what it represents in the system and why it matters for understanding the solution.
3. Looking back at your implementation, is there anything in this design you would change, and why?

**Sequence diagram:**

1. What user action or system event starts the sequence, and what is the expected outcome when it completes successfully?
2. Identify the 2--3 most important steps in the sequence. For each one, describe what is happening and note whether it involves existing code or new/modified code from your solution.
3. What error cases or alternative paths are not shown in the diagram, and why did you leave them out?

**Cross-cutting:**

4. If you used AI to create or check any part of the diagrams, describe what it produced, what you verified against the actual code, and what you had to correct or add. If AI was not used, write "N/A."
```

Grading (15 points): existing code 2, solution code 2, annotations 3, UML notation (relationships,
cardinality, lifelines; minor errors are fine) 2, Q&A 4, AI transparency 2. The Q&A points are for
understanding that goes beyond what the diagram already shows, so answer with reasons, not a
re-description of the boxes.

## Sprint report (D8) sections

`docs/sprint<N>/report.md`, following `docs/sprint0/report.md`:

- Team: names, GitHub usernames, project name, repository link.
- Sprint overview.
- Backlog: milestone link, why the team chose these issues, plus a table of title, owner, points,
  scope and status.
- Requirements and design: when specs were done, what surprised you, design rationale.
- Completed issues: title, owner, PR link, author, reviewer, what changed.
- Test strategy, including untestable changes and why.
- AI tool usage per member: tools, session count, AI log folder link, and 2–3 sentences on lessons
  learned.
- Release: tag and release link.
- Risks and retrospective: what worked, what slowed the team down, next-sprint changes.
- Next sprint plan: initial ideas and carryover issues.
- From Sprint 2: Sprint 1 carryovers (which were taken, which were skipped and why), and D6 and D7
  in the deliverables summary. The report covers this sprint's work only.

# AI assistance disclosure — required format

Course rule, not an upstream Gitea one. Every contributor discloses their own AI use per issue,
**even when no AI was used**. Source: the course AI Log Instructions page and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
(AI Contribution Policy). Two separate places, both required. The rest of the PR and issue
format is in `COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.

## 1. A comment on the issue

Posted by each contributor on the **issue** they worked, once their work is done. One comment per
person — never edit someone else's. Add later sessions by editing your own table.

```markdown
### AI Assistance — @your-github-username

**Role in this issue:** Implementation

| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-code | [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md) | Confirmed the files found during concept location, drafted the template change and tests, ran them |

**Attachments:** [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl/](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/tree/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl)
```

- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.

## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link

Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, logs are
referenced in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page, D5).

```markdown
## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5) drafted the handler and tests following the existing register/delete
code; I reviewed every line, ran the tests, checked the page by hand, and can explain each change.
AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.
```

Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log.

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
  the questions are for you.

## For AI agents drafting an issue or PR

Put section 2 in every PR description you draft, and draft the section 1 issue comment
separately, both filled in from the session you actually ran — never with placeholders. You may
draft the wording, but say plainly that the human must review and edit it before posting, and leave
the issue comment for them to post under their own account.

22dd91d797 Merge pull request #120 from CSCI-435-SE/feat/issue-117-group-notifications-by-repo
22dd91d797150d3c5350a145663c1627f98420d5
feat(notifications): sort notifications by reason or type (#52) CarsonRackley open feat/issue-52-sort-notifications-by-reason-or-type
Closes #52

## What changed

Every notification now stores **why** it was sent: Review requested, Assigned, Mentioned or Subscribed. The Notifications page has a new **Sort** dropdown with Newest (the default), Reason and Type, next to the Repository and Type filters. Each row except "Other" shows its reason as a small label.

- **Model** (`models/activities`):
  - `Notification` gets a `Reason` column. Its value is its rank: Other 0, Subscribed 1, Mentioned 2, Assigned 3, Review requested 4 (Decision 6).
  - When an event updates an existing notification, the reason only changes if the new one ranks higher (Decision 2), so a later comment doesn't turn "Review requested" into "Subscribed".
  - `FindNotificationOptions.Sort` adds `reason DESC` or `source` to the query's order. When #117's grouping is on, it applies after the repository name.
- **Migration** `v345`: adds `reason SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, so existing notifications are "Other" and nothing else about them changes (Decision 3).
- **Notification service** (`services/uinotification/notify.go`):
  - Each queue item carries a reason. Review requests, assignments and the mention lists set their own.
  - Items with no reason (the watchers and participants broadcast, and any items queued before the upgrade) are stored as Subscribed.
  - `NewPullRequest` used to put mentioned users in the same set as watchers. It now pushes them separately, so a mentioned watcher is stored as Mentioned.
  - Repository transfer notifications skip the queue and stay "Other", as AC1 now says.
- **Router** (`routers/web/user/notification.go`): `sort=reason` or `sort=type` is parsed into the existing `notificationFilter`, the same way #117 added `group`, so the purge redirect, the bulk action redirect and the in-place refresh keep it. Any other value is ignored, which means newest first.
- **Templates**:
  - The Sort dropdown is built like #50's filter dropdowns.
  - `sort` is added to every link that already carried `group`: the tabs, both filters, both "Clear filters" links, the purge form, the single-row status forms and the bulk URL. Pagination already carries it.
  - The reason label is in `notification_item.tmpl`, so the flat and grouped lists both show it.
  - 9 new strings in `locale_en-US.json`.

## Why

Notifications are one row per thread and didn't record why they were sent, so there was no way to put "your review is requested" ahead of "a repository you watch had a comment". This PR covers every acceptance criterion in #52:

- **AC1:** review requests, assignments, mentions and watching or participating store Review requested, Assigned, Mentioned and Subscribed. Repository transfers store Other.
- **AC2:** an existing notification only takes a reason that ranks higher.
- **AC3:** the migration gives existing notifications "Other" and changes nothing else.
- **AC4:** Sort: Reason orders Review requested, Assigned, Mentioned, Subscribed, Other, newest first inside each. Every row except "Other" shows its label.
- **AC5:** Sort: Type orders issues, pull requests, commits, repositories, newest first inside each.
- **AC6:** with no sort or an unknown one, the list is newest first, in the same order as before.
- **AC7:** `sort` survives tab switches, both filters, grouping on and off, paging, single-row read and pin, bulk actions, "Mark all as read" and the in-place refresh.
- **AC8:** with grouping on, sections stay A–Z and the sort applies inside each one.
- **AC9:** pinned notifications are sorted with the rest.

## How it was tested

### Test strategy

- **The ranking and the "only raise" rule** are model logic, so they're tested against the model.
- **Sorting** is a query, so it's also tested at the model level, with grouping and paging.
- **Parsing `sort` and building the redirect link** are pure functions, so they're unit tests.
- **Which event stores which reason** depends on the notifier, the queue and the model working together. In integration tests the queue is `immediate`, so those tests drive real service calls (a review request, an assignment, comments with and without a mention, a new pull request) and check the stored reason.
- **Whether every link and redirect keeps `sort`** only shows in the rendered page, so that's an integration test, built like #117's `LinksKeepGrouping`.

| AC | Test |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | Integration `TestNotificationReason`: `ReviewRequestedOutranksALaterComment`, `Assigned`, `MentionedAndSubscribed`, `MentionedWatcherOfANewPullRequest` (fails without the `NewPullRequest` change); `TestCreateOrUpdateIssueNotificationsReason` |
| AC2 | `TestCreateOrUpdateIssueNotificationsReason` (lower doesn't replace higher, higher does); integration `ReviewRequestedOutranksALaterComment` (a later comment keeps "Review requested") |
| AC3 | `Test_AddReasonToNotification` (every existing row is "Other"; every other column is unchanged) |
| AC4, AC9 | `TestFindNotificationsSort`; integration `TestNotificationSort/Reason` (order, labels, the pinned row sorted with the rest, the read tab) |
| AC5 | `TestFindNotificationsSort`; integration `TestNotificationSort/Type` |
| AC6 | `TestFindNotificationsSort` (no sort and an unknown sort); `TestParseNotificationFilter` (`?sort=bogus`); integration `NewestByDefaultWithLabels` |
| AC7 | `TestParseNotificationFilter`, `TestNotificationViewLink` (`sort` cases); integration `LinksKeepSort`, `InPlaceRefreshKeepsSort`, `RedirectsKeepSort` |
| AC8 | `TestFindNotificationsSort` (grouped, and across pages); integration `InsideRepositoryGroups` |

**Not covered automatically:** how the dropdown and labels look. The dropdown is the same Fomantic component as #50's filters. The screenshots below show it by hand.

## CI / manual verification

Run in WSL (Debian) on this branch:

- `go test` for `TestCreateOrUpdateIssueNotifications`, `TestCreateOrUpdateIssueNotificationsReason`, `TestFindNotificationsSort`, `TestFindNotificationsGroupByRepo`, `TestNotificationsForUser`, `TestCountNotificationsByRepo` (`./models/activities/`), and the notification tests in `./routers/web/user/`: pass.
- `make test-migration`: pass, including `Test_AddReasonToNotification`.
- `make test-integration#TestNotification`: pass. That's the 4 `TestNotificationReason` and 7 `TestNotificationSort` subtests, plus the existing `TestNotificationFilters` (#50), `TestNotificationBulkActions` (#51) and `TestNotificationGroupByRepo` (#117).
- Playwright `notification-bulk.test.ts` and `notification-group.test.ts` on Chromium and Firefox: 4/4 pass with the new dropdown and labels on the page.
- `make lint-go lint-templates lint-editorconfig`: clean.
- CI runs on this PR and must pass before merging.

## Design

Decisions 1–5 are in #52's spec, which controlled-opposition reviewed. Decisions 6–8 were added during implementation, each with its alternatives:

- **Decision 6:** store the reason as a number equal to its rank (from the spec review). Sorting is then `ORDER BY reason DESC`, and "only raise" is a single `>`.
- **Decision 7:** show the reason label in every sort, not only under Sort: Reason.
- **Decision 8:** pick the sort from a dropdown next to the filters.

The spec review's note 1 (repository transfers) is answered in AC1: they store "Other".

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- **A reason never goes back down** (Decision 2), so "Review requested" stays after the review is done or the request is removed. That's the trade-off the spec chose over tracking read state.
- **The reason numbers are part of the schema** (Decision 6). A future reason that should rank between two existing ones needs a migration to renumber.
- **Items in the notification queue during an upgrade** have no reason and are stored as Subscribed, as Decision 1 planned.

**Encountered:**
- **`UpdatedBy` never changes on an unread notification.**
  - `updateIssueNotification` (`models/activities/notification.go`) passes `"update_by"` to `Cols()`, but the column is `updated_by`, and xorm silently ignores the unknown name.
  - I confirmed it with a throwaway test: after an event by user 5, an unread notification still had `updated_by` 1.
  - It's outside #52, so I left it alone. It's worth its own bug issue.
- **Sort: Type's "Commits" group is always empty.** Gitea never creates commit notifications. #50's "Commits" filter has the same gap. I kept it so the sort follows the filter's order.
- **The pager's total still counts only the tab's status, not pinned rows** (noted in #120). Sorting doesn't change that.

## Screenshots

Taken on a throwaway local instance with sample data (two repositories, one notification per reason).

Sort notifications by reason or type CarsonRackley ['CarsonRackley'] Sprint 2
Part of #7. Related: #50 (filter by repository and type), #51 (bulk actions), #117 (group by repository). Carried over from Sprint 1.

### User Story

As a user with many notifications, I want to sort my notification list by why I was notified or by what it is about, so that the notifications that need me, such as review requests and assignments, come first and related notifications sit together.

### User Scenario

Sam comes back from a week off to 60 unread notifications. On the Notifications page he picks **Sort: Reason**. The two pull requests where his review was requested are at the top, each labelled "Review requested", then the issues assigned to him, then the threads where he was mentioned, then everything from repositories he watches. He works through the review requests first. He then turns on #117's **Group by repository**, and inside each repository's section the rows keep the same reason order. Finally he narrows to `org/backend` with #50's filter, selects the "Subscribed" rows and marks them read with #51's bulk bar. The sort stays the whole time, and the URL keeps it.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a user is requested to review a pull request, is assigned to an issue, is @-mentioned, or gets a notification only because they watch the repository or participate in the thread, when the notification is created, then it stores the reason "Review requested", "Assigned", "Mentioned" or "Subscribed" respectively. Repository transfer notifications, which are not created through the notification queue, store "Other".
- [ ] AC2: Given a notification already has a reason, when a new event updates the same notification with a different reason, then it keeps whichever reason ranks higher in the order Review requested > Assigned > Mentioned > Subscribed. For example, a comment on a pull request does not turn "Review requested" into "Subscribed".
- [ ] AC3: Given notifications that existed before this change, when the migration runs, then they get the reason "Other" and nothing else about them changes.
- [ ] AC4: Given the Notifications page, when the user picks **Sort: Reason**, then the rows are ordered Review requested, Assigned, Mentioned, Subscribed, Other, with newest first inside each reason. Each row except "Other" shows its reason as a label, in every sort (Decision 7).
- [ ] AC5: Given the Notifications page, when the user picks **Sort: Type**, then the rows are ordered Issues, Pull requests, Commits, Repository (the order of #50's type filter), with newest first inside each type.
- [ ] AC6: Given no sort is chosen, or an unknown `sort` value is in the URL, when the page loads, then the list is newest first exactly as it is today.
- [ ] AC7: Given a sort is chosen, when the user switches between Unread and Read, changes a #50 filter, turns #117's grouping on or off, moves to another page, marks or pins a single notification, runs a #51 bulk action, or the list refreshes in place, then the sort is still applied (`sort=reason` or `sort=type` is kept in the URL).
- [ ] AC8: Given #117's grouping is on and a sort is chosen, when the page loads, then the repository sections stay A–Z and the rows inside each section follow the chosen sort.
- [ ] AC9: Given pinned notifications, when a sort is chosen, then they are sorted with the rest of the rows, as #50 decided for filters.

### Out of Scope

- More reasons, such as "Author", "Commented", "State changed" or team mentions. They can follow in a later issue once the column exists.
- Changing the stored reason when a review request or assignment is removed. The reason only moves up.
- Filtering by reason, and reason sections like #117's repository sections.
- The notifications API (`/api/v1/notifications`) and email notifications.

### Open Questions

- Should the API expose the reason later, like GitHub's `reason` field? (Proposed: a follow-up issue, out of scope here.)
- ~~Which reason does a repository transfer notification get?~~ **Decided during implementation:** "Other". It doesn't go through the queue, and a new reason value is out of scope. Added to AC1.

### Design Decisions

#### Decision 1: Store the reason in a new column on the notification row

**Decision:** Add a `reason` column to the `notification` table, set by the event handlers in `services/uinotification` and passed through the notification queue into `CreateOrUpdateIssueNotifications`.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Work the reason out when the page is read, by joining assignees, review requests and comment mentions for each row. (b) A separate table with one row per reason per notification, so a notification can hold several reasons.
**Rationale:** The event handler is the only place that knows why a notification was sent. Working it out at read time needs several joins on every page load and still can't tell a mention from a subscription. A separate table answers "all reasons", which the sort doesn't need, and costs an extra join for one sortable value.
**Consequences:** It needs a migration and a change to the queued notification payload, so notifications still in the queue during an upgrade fall back to "Subscribed". Later reasons are a new value, not a schema change.

#### Decision 2: The highest-priority reason wins

**Decision:** When an event updates an existing notification, the stored reason only changes if the new reason ranks higher (Review requested > Assigned > Mentioned > Subscribed > Other).
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) The latest event's reason always overwrites. (b) Highest priority while unread, then start fresh once the notification is read.
**Rationale:** Notifications are one row per thread, so with (a) any later comment would demote a pending review request to "Subscribed", which defeats sorting by reason. (b) is more precise but adds read-state logic and tests for little gain this sprint.
**Consequences:** A reason can stay higher than the latest event, for example "Review requested" after the review is done. Removing a request doesn't lower it (Out of Scope).

#### Decision 3: Existing notifications get "Other", sorted last

**Decision:** The migration adds the column with a default of "Other", and new events fill in real reasons from then on.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Default existing rows to "Subscribed". (b) Backfill reasons in the migration from current assignees and review requests.
**Rationale:** We don't know why an existing notification was sent, so labelling it "Subscribed" would be wrong for old review requests. A backfill is a heavier, riskier migration and still can't recover mentions.
**Consequences:** Right after an upgrade, most rows sort under "Other" until new activity updates them. Because of Decision 2, any new event moves a row out of "Other".

#### Decision 4: Offer both Sort: Reason and Sort: Type

**Decision:** The sort menu has Newest (the default), Reason and Type.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Reason only, since #50's type filter already answers "show me pull requests". (b) Type only, which needs no migration or queue change.
**Rationale:** The issue asks for both. Type sorting reuses the existing `Source` column, so it adds almost no work once the sort parameter exists, and it orders the full list, which a filter doesn't. Type only would drop the reason part, which is the point of the issue, and would shrink it to a small issue.
**Consequences:** Two orderings to test across tabs, filters, grouping and paging, and the menu has three choices instead of two.

#### Decision 5: Sorting works inside #117's repository groups

**Decision:** `sort` is its own URL parameter, kept everywhere `repo`, `source` and `group` are kept. With grouping on, the sections stay A–Z and the rows inside each section follow the chosen sort.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Choosing a sort turns grouping off, so there is only one ordering at a time. (b) Sort by reason shows its own section headers per reason, like #117's repository sections.
**Rationale:** Grouping and sorting answer different questions, "which project" and "what needs me first", and the user scenario uses both together. (a) would silently undo a choice the user made. (b) is the most work and would need nested headers when grouping is also on.
**Consequences:** With grouping on, the query orders by repository first, then by the chosen sort, then newest first. Every link and redirect that carries `group` from #117 also has to carry `sort`.

#### Decision 6: Store the reason as a number that matches its rank

*Added during implementation, from the spec review.*

**Decision:** `reason` is a `SMALLINT` whose value is its rank: Other 0, Subscribed 1, Mentioned 2, Assigned 3, Review requested 4. The migration's default of 0 is "Other".
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A short string such as `"review_requested"`, mapped to a rank in Go. (b) Numbers in the order the reasons were added, with a `CASE` expression for the sort.
**Rationale:** With the rank as the value, Sort: Reason is `ORDER BY reason DESC`, and Decision 2's "only raise" rule is a single `>` comparison. Both stay in the database, so paging and #117's grouping work unchanged. (a) needs a `CASE` in the query or sorting in memory, which breaks paging. (b) has the same `CASE` problem.
**Consequences:** The numbers are part of the schema. A later reason has to fit into the ranking, which may mean renumbering in a migration. The value is never shown, so the order only matters for sorting.

#### Decision 7: Show the reason label in every sort

*Added during implementation.*

**Decision:** Every row except "Other" shows its reason as a label, whichever sort is chosen, including the default.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Show it only under Sort: Reason, the narrowest reading of AC4. (b) Show it as tooltip text on the row's icon.
**Rationale:** Why you were notified matters even in the newest-first list, and GitHub shows it the same way. (a) hides it unless the user already knows to sort by it. (b) makes it invisible on touch screens and to anyone who doesn't hover.
**Consequences:** The default list now has labels on new notifications, so AC6 covers only the order of the default list, not its markup.

#### Decision 8: Pick the sort from a dropdown next to the filters

*Added during implementation.*

**Decision:** A "Sort" dropdown with Newest, Reason and Type, built like #50's Repository and Type filter dropdowns.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Three toggle buttons next to #117's "Group by repository" button. (b) Sortable column headers.
**Rationale:** A sort is one choice out of several, which a dropdown shows best, and copying #50's dropdown keeps the toolbar consistent. (a) takes more room for a setting that is used rarely. (b) doesn't fit, because the list is rows of cards, not a table.
**Consequences:** The dropdown's links carry `repo`, `source` and `group`, the same as the filters' links do.

### Scope

medium. Both sorts ship in one PR. The reason set is kept to four values (review requested, assigned, mentioned, subscribed) plus "Other" for older rows, to stay medium.

---
Drafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5).

func updateIssueNotification(ctx context.Context, userID, issueID, commentID, updatedByID int64, reason NotificationReason) error {
	notification, err := GetIssueNotification(ctx, userID, issueID)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	// NOTICE: Only update comment id when the before notification on this issue is read, otherwise you may miss some old comments.
	// But we need update update_by so that the notification will be reorder
	var cols []string
	if notification.Status == NotificationStatusRead {
		notification.Status = NotificationStatusUnread
		notification.CommentID = commentID
		cols = []string{"status", "update_by", "comment_id"}
	} else {
		notification.UpdatedBy = updatedByID
		cols = []string{"update_by"}
	}
	if reason > notification.Reason { // the reason only rises, so a later comment doesn't bury a review request
		notification.Reason = reason
		cols = append(cols, "reason")
	}

	_, err = db.GetEngine(ctx).ID(notification.ID).Cols(cols...).Update(notification)
	return err
}

// GetIssueNotification return the notification about an issue
func GetIssueNotification(ctx context.Context, userID, issueID int64) (*Notification, error) {
----

const (
	// NotificationStatusUnread represents an unread notification
	NotificationStatusUnread NotificationStatus = iota + 1
	// NotificationStatusRead represents a read notification
	NotificationStatusRead
	// NotificationStatusPinned represents a pinned notification
	NotificationStatusPinned
)

const (
	// NotificationSourceIssue is a notification of an issue
	NotificationSourceIssue NotificationSource = iota + 1
	// NotificationSourcePullRequest is a notification of a pull request
	NotificationSourcePullRequest
	// NotificationSourceCommit is a notification of a commit
	NotificationSourceCommit
	// NotificationSourceRepository is a notification for a repository
	NotificationSourceRepository
)


		issueWatches, err := issues_model.GetIssueWatchersIDs(ctx, issueID, true)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		toNotify.AddMultiple(issueWatches...)
		if !(issue.IsPull && issues_model.HasWorkInProgressPrefix(issue.Title)) {
			repoWatches, err := repo_model.GetRepoWatchersIDs(ctx, issue.RepoID)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			toNotify.AddMultiple(repoWatches...)
		}
		issueParticipants, err := issue.GetParticipantIDsByIssue(ctx)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		toNotify.AddMultiple(issueParticipants...)

		// don't notify user who cause notification
		delete(toNotify, notificationAuthorID)
		// explicit unwatch on issue
		issueUnWatches, err := issues_model.GetIssueWatchersIDs(ctx, issueID, false)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		for _, id := range issueUnWatches {
			toNotify.Remove(id)
		}
	}

	err = issue.LoadRepo(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	// notify
	for userID := range toNotify {
		issue.Repo.Units = nil
		user, err := user_model.GetUserByID(ctx, userID)
		if err != nil {
			if user_model.IsErrUserNotExist(err) {
				continue
			}

			return err
		}
		if issue.IsPull && !access_model.CheckRepoUnitUser(ctx, issue.Repo, user, unit.TypePullRequests) {
			continue
		}
		if !issue.IsPull && !access_model.CheckRepoUnitUser(ctx, issue.Repo, user, unit.TypeIssues) {
			continue
		}

		if notificationExists(notifications, issue.ID, userID) {
			if err = updateIssueNotification(ctx, userID, issue.ID, commentID, notificationAuthorID, reason); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			continue
		}
		if err = createIssueNotification(ctx, userID, issue, commentID, notificationAuthorID, reason); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

package integration

import (
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	activities_model "gitea.dev/models/activities"
	"gitea.dev/models/db"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	"gitea.dev/modules/test"
	issue_service "gitea.dev/services/issue"
	notify_service "gitea.dev/services/notify"
	"gitea.dev/tests"

	"github.com/PuerkitoBio/goquery"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// the notification queue is immediate in tests, so each event has stored its notifications when the call returns
func TestNotificationReason(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()

	// user4 watches user2/repo1; user5 doesn't
	user2 := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
	user4 := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 4})
	repo1 := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
	reasonOf := func(userID, issueID int64) activities_model.NotificationReason {
		return unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &activities_model.Notification{UserID: userID, IssueID: issueID}).Reason
	}
	loadIssue := func(id int64) *issues_model.Issue {
		issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: id})
		require.NoError(t, issue.LoadAttributes(t.Context())) // the services read issue.Repo
		return issue
	}

	t.Run("ReviewRequestedOutranksALaterComment", func(t *testing.T) {
		pull := loadIssue(2)
		_, err := issue_service.ReviewRequest(t.Context(), pull, user2, nil, user4, true)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		assert.Equal(t, activities_model.NotificationReasonReviewRequested, reasonOf(4, pull.ID)) // #52 AC1

		_, err = issue_service.CreateIssueComment(t.Context(), user2, repo1, pull, "a comment every watcher hears about", nil)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		assert.Equal(t, activities_model.NotificationReasonReviewRequested, reasonOf(4, pull.ID)) // #52 AC2
	})

	t.Run("Assigned", func(t *testing.T) {
		issue := loadIssue(5)
		removed, _, err := issue_service.ToggleAssigneeWithNotify(t.Context(), issue, user2, user4.ID)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.False(t, removed)
		assert.Equal(t, activities_model.NotificationReasonAssigned, reasonOf(4, issue.ID)) // #52 AC1
	})

	t.Run("MentionedAndSubscribed", func(t *testing.T) {
		issue := loadIssue(1)
		_, err := issue_service.CreateIssueComment(t.Context(), user2, repo1, issue, "cc @user5", nil)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		assert.Equal(t, activities_model.NotificationReasonMentioned, reasonOf(5, issue.ID))  // #52 AC1
		assert.Equal(t, activities_model.NotificationReasonSubscribed, reasonOf(4, issue.ID)) // #52 AC1 a watcher
	})

	t.Run("MentionedWatcherOfANewPullRequest", func(t *testing.T) {
		pr, err := issues_model.GetPullRequestByIssueID(t.Context(), 3)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		notify_service.NewPullRequest(t.Context(), pr, []*user_model.User{user4})              // user4 is both a watcher and mentioned
		assert.Equal(t, activities_model.NotificationReasonMentioned, reasonOf(4, pr.IssueID)) // #52 AC1
	})
}

func TestNotificationSort(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()

	// user2's notifications: #2 read, #3 pinned and #4 unread in user2/repo1, #5 unread in user2/repo2; #5 is the newest
	set := func(id int64, reason activities_model.NotificationReason, source activities_model.NotificationSource) {
		_, err := db.GetEngine(t.Context()).ID(id).Cols("reason", "source").NoAutoTime().Update(&activities_model.Notification{Reason: reason, Source: source}) // keeps the fixtures' times, which set the newest-first order
		require.NoError(t, err)
	}
	set(2, activities_model.NotificationReasonSubscribed, activities_model.NotificationSourceIssue)
	set(3, activities_model.NotificationReasonReviewRequested, activities_model.NotificationSourcePullRequest)
	set(4, activities_model.NotificationReasonOther, activities_model.NotificationSourceIssue)
	set(5, activities_model.NotificationReasonMentioned, activities_model.NotificationSourceIssue)

	session := loginUser(t, "user2")
	type row struct{ ID, Reason string }
	rowsAt := func(t *testing.T, link string) ([]row, *HTMLDoc) {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", link), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		var rows []row
		doc.doc.Find("#notification_table .notifications-item").Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) {
			rows = append(rows, row{s.AttrOr("id", ""), strings.TrimSpace(s.Find(".notification-reason").Text())})
		})
		return rows, doc
	}

	t.Run("Reason", func(t *testing.T) {
		rows, doc := rowsAt(t, "/notifications?sort=reason")
		assert.Equal(t, []row{
			{"notification_3", "Review requested"}, // #52 AC9 the pinned row sorts with the rest
			{"notification_5", "Mentioned"},
			{"notification_4", ""}, // #52 AC4 "Other" has no label
		}, rows)
		assert.Equal(t, "Sort: Reason", strings.TrimSpace(doc.doc.Find(`[data-test-id="notification-sort"] > .text`).Text()))

		rows, _ = rowsAt(t, "/notifications?type=read&sort=reason")
		assert.Equal(t, []row{{"notification_3", "Review requested"}, {"notification_2", "Subscribed"}}, rows)
	})

	t.Run("Type", func(t *testing.T) {
		rows, _ := rowsAt(t, "/notifications?sort=type")
		assert.Equal(t, []row{{"notification_5", "Mentioned"}, {"notification_4", ""}, {"notification_3", "Review requested"}}, rows) // #52 AC5 issues, then pull requests
	})

	t.Run("NewestByDefaultWithLabels", func(t *testing.T) {
		rows, doc := rowsAt(t, "/notifications?sort=bogus")
		assert.Equal(t, []row{{"notification_5", "Mentioned"}, {"notification_4", ""}, {"notification_3", "Review requested"}}, rows) // #52 AC6, and Decision 7's labels
		assert.Equal(t, "Sort", strings.TrimSpace(doc.doc.Find(`[data-test-id="notification-sort"] > .text`).Text()))
	})

	t.Run("InsideRepositoryGroups", func(t *testing.T) {
		rows, doc := rowsAt(t, "/notifications?group=repo&sort=reason")
		assert.Equal(t, []row{{"notification_3", "Review requested"}, {"notification_4", ""}, {"notification_5", "Mentioned"}}, rows) // #52 AC8
		assert.Equal(t, 2, doc.doc.Find(".notification-group").Length())
	})

	t.Run("LinksKeepSort", func(t *testing.T) {
		_, doc := rowsAt(t, "/notifications?sort=reason&group=repo&source=issue&perPage=1") // two pages, so there are pagination links
		for _, c := range []struct{ selector, attr string }{
			{".small-menu-items a.item", "href"}, // Unread and Read tabs
			{`[data-test-id="notification-filter-repo"] .menu a.item`, "href"},
			{`[data-test-id="notification-filter-type"] .menu a.item`, "href"},
			{`[data-test-id="notification-group-repo"]`, "href"},
			{".pagination a.item[href]", "href"},
			{"form.notifications-buttons", "action"}, // single-row status actions
			{"#notification_div", "data-bulk-url"},
		} {
			found := doc.doc.Find(c.selector)
			require.NotZero(t, found.Length(), c.selector)
			found.Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) {
				assert.Contains(t, s.AttrOr(c.attr, ""), "sort=reason", c.selector) // #52 AC7
			})
		}
		clearFilters := doc.doc.Find(".flex-text-block a.ui.button").FilterFunction(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) bool {
			return strings.TrimSpace(s.Text()) == "Clear filters"
		})
		assert.Equal(t, "/notifications?group=repo&sort=reason", clearFilters.AttrOr("href", "")) // a view setting, not a filter

		var sortLinks []string
		doc.doc.Find(`[data-test-id="notification-sort"] .menu a.item`).Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) {
			sortLinks = append(sortLinks, s.AttrOr("href", ""))
		})
		assert.Equal(t, []string{
			"/notifications?source=issue&group=repo",
			"/notifications?source=issue&group=repo&sort=reason",
			"/notifications?source=issue&group=repo&sort=type",
		}, sortLinks)
	})

	t.Run("InPlaceRefreshKeepsSort", func(t *testing.T) {
		rows, _ := rowsAt(t, "/notifications?sort=reason&div-only=true")
		assert.Equal(t, "notification_3", rows[0].ID)

		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", "/notifications/status?type=unread&page=1&sort=reason", map[string]string{
			"notification_id":     "4",
			"notification_action": "pin",
		}), http.StatusOK)
		var ids []string
		NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body).doc.Find("#notification_table .notifications-item").Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) {
			ids = append(ids, s.AttrOr("id", ""))
		})
		assert.Equal(t, []string{"notification_3", "notification_5", "notification_4"}, ids) // #52 AC7 still by reason
	})

	t.Run("RedirectsKeepSort", func(t *testing.T) {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", "/notifications/bulk?type=read&sort=type", map[string]string{
			"action":           "mark_as_unread",
			"notification_ids": "2",
		}), http.StatusOK)
		redirect := test.ParseJSONRedirect(resp.Body.Bytes()).Redirect
		require.NotNil(t, redirect)
		assert.Equal(t, "/notifications?sort=type&type=read", *redirect) // #52 AC7

		resp = session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "POST", "/notifications/purge?sort=type"), http.StatusSeeOther)
		assert.Equal(t, "/notifications?sort=type", test.RedirectURL(resp))
	})
}

feat(notifications): store why each notification was sent and sort by reason or type (#52)
Notifications now store a reason: review requested, assigned, mentioned or
subscribed, ranked in that order. The event handlers in uinotification set
it on each queue item, and an existing notification only takes a reason that
ranks higher, so a later comment doesn't bury a review request. Migration 345
adds the column with "Other" for existing rows; repository transfers, which
skip the queue, are "Other" too.
The Notifications page gets a Sort dropdown (Newest, Reason, Type). The sort
is kept in the URL like #117's grouping, and applies inside each repository
when grouped. Every row except "Other" shows its reason as a label.

func (ns *notificationService) NewIssue(ctx context.Context, issue *issues_model.Issue, mentions []*user_model.User) {
	_ = ns.issueQueue.Push(issueNotificationOpts{
		IssueID:              issue.ID,
		NotificationAuthorID: issue.Poster.ID,
	})
	for _, mention := range mentions {
		_ = ns.issueQueue.Push(issueNotificationOpts{
			IssueID:              issue.ID,
			NotificationAuthorID: issue.Poster.ID,
			ReceiverID:           mention.ID,
			Reason:               activities_model.NotificationReasonMentioned,
		})
	}
}

func (ns *notificationService) IssueChangeStatus(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, commitID string, issue *issues_model.Issue, actionComment *issues_model.Comment, isClosed bool) {

func (ns *notificationService) PullReviewDismiss(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, review *issues_model.Review, comment *issues_model.Comment) {
	opts := issueNotificationOpts{
		IssueID:              review.IssueID,
		NotificationAuthorID: doer.ID,
		CommentID:            comment.ID,
	}
	_ = ns.issueQueue.Push(opts)
}

func (ns *notificationService) IssueChangeAssignee(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, issue *issues_model.Issue, assignee *user_model.User, removed bool, comment *issues_model.Comment) {
	if !removed && doer.ID != assignee.ID {
		opts := issueNotificationOpts{
			IssueID:              issue.ID,
			NotificationAuthorID: doer.ID,
			ReceiverID:           assignee.ID,
			Reason:               activities_model.NotificationReasonAssigned,
		}

		if comment != nil {
			opts.CommentID = comment.ID
		}

		_ = ns.issueQueue.Push(opts)
	}
}

func (ns *notificationService) PullRequestReviewRequest(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, issue *issues_model.Issue, reviewer *user_model.User, isRequest bool, comment *issues_model.Comment) {
	if isRequest {
		opts := issueNotificationOpts{
			IssueID:              issue.ID,
			NotificationAuthorID: doer.ID,
			ReceiverID:           reviewer.ID,
			Reason:               activities_model.NotificationReasonReviewRequested,
